editorial:
Imagine moving into your first New York City place only to find out you have a few thousand roommates you never asked for. That is exactly what happens to Joe, a sweet guy who just wants a fresh start. Instead of a quiet home, he gets a dump filled with singing and dancing cockroaches. It sounds gross, but the movie plays it for laughs, turning a nightmare scenario into a weirdly heartwarming buddy comedy. The vibe is totally wacky and fast, making you root for Joe even as he deals with the chaos of these bug guests who just want to party.

The best part is definitely the music and the way the bugs interact with the real world. While some of the effects look a bit dated now, the humor still lands because the acting is so earnest. If you like movies that are just plain odd and fun, you will love this. It is a great pick for a lazy Friday night. You can find it for rent on Apple TV or stream it on Prime Video. If you are a collector who loves weird 90s gems, adding the Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: In the end, Joe decides to embrace his bug friends instead of trying to kill them. He helps the cockroaches fight off a greedy landlord who wants to tear the building down. After a big, musical showdown, the bugs and Joe form a real bond. They realize they can coexist and support each other. Everything wraps up with Joe finally feeling at home in the city, knowing he has a huge, weird family looking out for him.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves weird 90s comedies and musical numbers.
